clue.text: Scratching head, Joy embraces a certain female with pride

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping around the other piece, which sits inside
scratching out the head of a word means its first letter is struck off

parts.note: joy means bliss
the head of the word for joy is its first letter, struck off
a certain person or thing is a particular one, so 'a certain' gives one

explanation.surface: A woman named Joy, scratching her head, hugs a certain proud lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' wraps the trimmed joy around the piece for 'a certain'. 'Pride' looks like a feeling but is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called a pride, so a female member of one is the she-lion.

clue.text: Set off without a meal

indicators.note: without here means leaving out the letter that follows it

parts.note: to set off a rocket or venture is to launch it

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey without eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is the everyday sense of the word.

clue.text: To Riga, migrating without paperwork

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of 'within the bounds of', the run of letters lying across the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of To through Riga into the start of migrating

explanation.surface: Someone migrates to Riga without the proper documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without paperwork' reads as lacking papers; the definition is 'paperwork' alone, in the sense of work done with paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding paper into shapes is literally work in paper, a playful reading of a bureaucratic word.

clue.text: Real origins of European common toad probed by Henry

indicators.note: being probed means having something pushed inside, so the next piece goes in
the origins of words are their first letters

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Is the common European toad genuinely being examined by a man named Henry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'probed by' puts H inside ECT, the first letters of European, common and toad.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-borrowed word means genuine or authentic, a direct synonym of real.

clue.text: Coatis cling and spit, unusually obstructive course of action

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Coatis behaving oddly by clinging and spitting at people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges all fifteen letters of COATIS CLING and SPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics meant only to wreck an opponent's plans are an obstructive way of proceeding.

clue.text: Saw man chasing British online commentator

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a man who fells trees with a saw is a logger

explanation.surface: A lumberjack runs after a British pundit who writes online.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes a web log of opinions is a commentator publishing online.

clue.text: Singer tries to rebel after ban on underwear on beach

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so this comes first
after means the following piece comes behind the earlier ones
again one piece sitting on the next in a down entry, so it comes before it

parts.note: to bar is to ban
a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: letters that rebel refuse their usual order and are rearranged

parts.note: sand stands for the beach

explanation.surface: A singer rebels against a ban on wearing underwear at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebel' rearranges 'tries'; in a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the pieces stack in the order ban, underwear, rebels, beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbra Streisand is a famous American singer and actress.

clue.text: Once oddly tense and thin, resembling a stop sign

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first and third

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a thin, bony figure is angular

explanation.surface: Someone was once strangely tense and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop signs are regular eight-sided shapes, so something like one has eight angles.

clue.text: First to grow more delicate Alpine flower?

indicators.note: first to a word means its opening letter

parts.note: lacier means finer, more delicate, like lace

explanation.surface: Which Alpine bloom grows first and is the most delicate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, not a bloom; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of ice slowly flows down an Alpine valley, making it a flower in the punning sense.

clue.text: Half-heartedly withdraw commercial for tyre

indicators.note: half-heartedly removes half of the two-letter heart of the word, one of its middle pair

parts.note: to withdraw is to retire
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Half-heartedly pulling an advert for tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: RETIRE has heart IR; 'Half-heartedly' drops the I, leaving RETRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A worn tyre given a new tread is a remould, commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Are next to improbably huge robin

indicators.note: improbably signals an unlikely arrangement of the letters, an anagram

explanation.surface: There is an improbably huge robin right next to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improbably' rearranges HUGE ROBIN. The definition is a verb: to border on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To border or adjoin something is the verb sense, being next door to it.

clue.text: Reportedly followed progress of parcel

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word sounds like the spoken one

parts.note: to follow the progress of a parcel is to have tracked it

explanation.surface: Someone apparently tracked the progress of a parcel in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel' is a parcel of land, not a package.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel of land is an area or stretch of ground.

clue.text: A bit of a kip after extremes of heartache and passion

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the kip is the currency of Laos, divided into 100 at, so an at is a bit of one

explanation.surface: After the heartache and passion, a short nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' looks like British slang for a nap; here it is the Laotian currency, whose hundredth part is the at.
explanation.definitionFit: In the heat of the moment means at the height of passion: intensity of feeling.

clue.text: Cook it with fennel or with spinach

definitions.note: a menu adjective describing a dish served with spinach

indicators.note: to cook letters is to cook the books, altering them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook it with fennel, or with spinach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges IT and FENNEL OR; 'with spinach' is the definition, a culinary term.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes described in the style of Florence, such as eggs florentine, are served on a bed of spinach.

clue.text: "Pay me later!", ordered Co-operative worker

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker at the Co-op demanded to be paid later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges PAY ME LATER. The Co-op is a British chain of shops, so 'Co-operative' looks like a store name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works well with colleagues for the group's sake is co-operative.

clue.text: According to hearsay, ogle slim woman

indicators.note: hearsay is what is heard, so the letters match the sound of the spoken words

parts.note: to ogle is to eye, and slim is lean

explanation.surface: Gossip says someone ogles a slim woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands for the solution, a common crossword device.

clue.text: Team keeping discontented rattlesnake by itself

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: discontented means with the contents, the inner letters, removed

explanation.surface: A team keeps an unhappy rattlesnake all on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' empties rattlesnake to its two outside letters, which 'keeping' holds in the team. 'by itself' means multiplied by itself, not alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A number multiplied by itself is raised to the second power.

clue.text: It gets under the feet of two mums, trapped by routine

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
mum means quiet, giving sh, and mum is also mother, giving ma

explanation.surface: Something that keeps getting under the feet of two mothers stuck in a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts SH and MA, the two senses of 'mum', inside RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor covering woven from reeds is literally underfoot.

clue.text: Child's hero ignoring case of betrayal

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, so these are dropped

parts.note: treachery means betrayal

explanation.surface: A child's hero, overlooking a case of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' is the novelist Lee Child, not a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Reacher is the hero of Lee Child's thriller novels.

clue.text: Took bung for throwing match

parts.note: to take a photograph is to shoot it, so took gives shot
to bung something somewhere is British slang for to put it there

explanation.surface: Someone took a bribe to throw a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bung' looks like a bribe and 'throwing' like fixing a match; bung is British slang for put, and the match is an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: The athletics event of heaving a heavy metal ball is a throwing contest.

clue.text: Partly malarial Torcello, a Venetian island

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Torcello, an island in the Venetian lagoon, was once partly malarial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the island district of Venice around its famous bridge and market.

clue.text: Stars in east, south and west in conjunction

indicators.note: in means the compass points go inside the other word

parts.note: than is a conjunction in grammar, as in 'taller than me'
E is the compass abbreviation for east
S is the compass abbreviation for south
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Stars line up in the east, south and west, as astrologers say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conjunction' sounds astronomical; 'conjunction' is a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnus, a northern constellation, is a group of stars also known by this name.

clue.text: Incensed at people rejecting seconds, start to convulse and twitch

indicators.note: the second letter of each of the two words is thrown out
the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone furious at people turning down second helpings starts to convulse and twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting seconds' drops the second letters of 'at' and 'people', leaving A and POPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone purple with fury looks fit to burst a blood vessel, so incensed fits.

clue.text: Runs into Hebrew sage, perhaps

indicators.note: into means going inside the other piece

parts.note: Heb is the standard abbreviation for Hebrew
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Hebrew sage runs into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like a wise man; it is the plant, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is one example of a culinary plant used for flavouring.

clue.text: Nice article supporting young male scientist

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a boy is a young male
le is a French article, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A pleasant newspaper piece backs a young male scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant' but is the French city, so its article is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Boyle was the seventeenth-century chemist behind the gas-pressure law.

clue.text: Grumpy pal with piles first delivers annual greeting

indicators.note: first means this piece goes at the front

parts.note: piles of things means a great many
Grumpy and Happy are two of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, so a pal of Grumpy is Happy
a jury delivers or returns a verdict

explanation.surface: A grumpy friend suffering from piles still delivers a birthday greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grumpy' looks like a mood but is the dwarf, whose companion is Happy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional wish said on someone's birthday each year.

clue.text: See 23 down
Sick brother leaves NY street after thief's confession

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the other

parts.note: a thief owning up might say I nab

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of the word that follows

parts.note: Broadway is a famous New York street

explanation.surface: A brother falls ill and leaves New York after a thief admits everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seriously ill or in poor condition is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: See 23
Poet describing you poetically as "first in her field"

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the poet's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet
ye is an old poetic form of you

explanation.surface: A poet addresses a woman as 'you', calling her the best in her field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior or most respected woman in a profession is its leading figure.
